question: In Home Alone, what is the first name of the boy accidentally left behind when his family flies to Paris?
hint: His last name is McCallister.
funFact: The McCallister house is a real home in Winnetka, a suburb of Chicago.

question: Tradition says that if you're caught standing under which plant, you owe someone a kiss?
hint: It grows in clumps high up on tree branches.
funFact: Mistletoe is partly parasitic: it grows on trees and steals water and nutrients from its host.

question: At Mexican Christmas parties, blindfolded kids take turns swinging a stick at a star-shaped, candy-filled papier-mâché figure. What is it called?
hint: It hangs from a rope and bursts open when it breaks.
funFact: The classic Christmas piñata is a star with seven points, often said to stand for the seven deadly sins.

question: According to the song, what is Frosty the Snowman's nose made of?
hint: Think of something sewn onto a coat.
funFact: In the song, it's an old silk hat that brings Frosty to life.

question: In A Christmas Carol, what is the name of Bob Cratchit's sickly little son?
hint: He says, “God bless us, every one!”
funFact: Charles Dickens published the story in December 1843, and the first printing sold out by Christmas Eve.

question: Which holiday movie features the famous warning, “You'll shoot your eye out”?
hint: Ralphie dreams of a Red Ryder BB gun.
funFact: The film's narrator is humorist Jean Shepherd, whose stories inspired the movie.

question: In The Nightmare Before Christmas, what is the name of Halloween Town's Pumpkin King?
hint: His ghost dog is named Zero.
funFact: Tim Burton dreamed up the story, but the 1993 film was directed by Henry Selick, and composer Danny Elfman sang Jack's songs.

question: In Elf, what sweet topping does Buddy pour all over his spaghetti?
hint: It comes from trees, and Vermont and Canada are famous for it.
funFact: Buddy says the four main elf food groups are candy, candy canes, candy corn and syrup.

question: What do children hang up on Christmas Eve, hoping Santa will fill them?
hint: They're usually hung by the fireplace.
funFact: In a popular retelling of the St. Nicholas legend, gold he tossed in for three poor sisters landed in stockings hung by the fire to dry.

question: Every year, a giant Christmas tree is lit above the famous ice rink at which New York City landmark?
hint: It's named after a famously rich oil family.
funFact: The tradition began in 1931, when construction workers put up a small tree decorated with cranberries, paper garlands and even tin cans.

question: What hook-shaped, red-and-white striped peppermint treat is often hung on Christmas trees?
hint: Turn it upside down and it looks like the letter J.
funFact: The popular tale that a choirmaster in Cologne, Germany, invented them in 1670 has never been backed up by evidence.

question: In which animated Tom Hanks movie does a boy board a magical train to visit Santa on Christmas Eve?
hint: It's based on a picture book by Chris Van Allsburg.
funFact: Tom Hanks played several roles in the 2004 film, including the Conductor, the hobo and Santa.

question: Finish the lyric from “Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town”: “He's making a list and…”
hint: He wants to be sure he hasn't made any mistakes.
funFact: J. Fred Coots and Haven Gillespie wrote the song in 1934.

question: What thick, creamy holiday drink is often topped with nutmeg and spiked with rum or bourbon?
hint: It's sold in cartons in the dairy aisle every December.
funFact: In 1826, whiskey smuggled in for eggnog sparked West Point's “Eggnog Riot,” and around 20 cadets were court-martialed.

question: Besides cookies for Santa, what vegetable do many kids leave out for the reindeer?
hint: It's orange and crunchy, and bunnies love it too.
funFact: In the UK, Santa often gets a mince pie and a glass of sherry instead of milk and cookies.

question: Because of the way ice crystals form, almost every snowflake has how many arms or points?
hint: The same number as the legs on an insect.
funFact: Vermont farmer Wilson “Snowflake” Bentley took the first photograph of a single snowflake in 1885.

question: In How the Grinch Stole Christmas, how many sizes does the Grinch's small heart grow?
hint: As many as the blind mice in the nursery rhyme.
funFact: Dr. Seuss published the book in 1957.

question: In It's a Wonderful Life, what happens every time a bell rings?
hint: Little Zuzu says the line in the final scene.
funFact: The 1946 film disappointed at the box office and became a classic thanks to TV reruns.

question: Finish the lyric from “The Christmas Song”: “Chestnuts roasting on an open fire, Jack Frost nipping at your…”
hint: It's the part of your face that turns red in the cold.
funFact: Mel Tormé and Bob Wells wrote it in 1945, and Nat King Cole's recording made it a standard.

question: What is the December countdown calendar called that has a little door to open each day before Christmas?
hint: It's named after the church season leading up to Christmas.
funFact: Printed versions caught on in early-1900s Germany; printer Gerhard Lang is often credited with the first.

question: Finish the carol lyric: “Deck the halls with boughs of…”
hint: A spiky evergreen with bright red berries.
funFact: Thomas Oliphant's original 1862 English words said “Deck the hall,” just one hall.

question: Which Home Improvement star accidentally becomes Santa in the 1994 movie The Santa Clause?
hint: He also voices Buzz Lightyear.
funFact: He returned to the role nearly 30 years later in the Disney+ series The Santa Clauses (2022).

question: What spiced dough is used to build edible Christmas houses decorated with icing and candy?
hint: Its key spice comes from a knobbly root.
funFact: Gingerbread houses became popular in 19th-century Germany, helped along by the Grimms' fairy tale “Hansel and Gretel.”

question: In Australia, Christmas falls during which season?
hint: It's in the Southern Hemisphere.
funFact: Many Australians celebrate with a barbecue or seafood lunch, and plenty head to the beach.

question: In “’Twas the Night Before Christmas,” the children were nestled all snug in their beds while visions of what danced in their heads?
hint: A fairy in The Nutcracker is named after them.
funFact: Despite the name, sugarplums usually had no plums in them; they were small sugar-coated candies.

question: In which 1947 classic does a department-store Santa named Kris Kringle go on trial to prove he's the real thing?
hint: It's set around Macy's in New York City.
funFact: Edmund Gwenn won an Oscar for playing Kris Kringle.

question: Which Christmas ballet features a girl named Clara, a toy soldier prince and a battle with the Mouse King?
hint: The title character is a wooden toy with a powerful jaw.
funFact: It's based on E.T.A. Hoffmann's 1816 story “The Nutcracker and the Mouse King.”

question: In Britain, Santa Claus is traditionally known by what other name?
hint: Two words. Old pictures often show him in a long green robe.
funFact: Father Christmas began as a separate English figure who stood for Christmas cheer, and later merged with Santa.

question: According to the Bible, what three gifts did the Wise Men bring to baby Jesus?
hint: One is a precious metal; the other two are fragrant tree resins.
funFact: The Bible never says there were three wise men; the number comes from the three gifts.

question: In “We Wish You a Merry Christmas,” what kind of pudding do the carolers demand?
hint: It's a steamed British pudding, a lot like Christmas pudding.
funFact: The carolers refuse to leave: “We won't go until we get some!”

question: Which TV channel is famous for its “Countdown to Christmas” lineup of cozy made-for-TV holiday movies?
hint: Its logo features a little crown.
funFact: Hallmark began as a greeting-card business, founded in Kansas City in 1910.

question: Which red-and-green Christmas plant has bright red “petals” that are actually leaves?
hint: It's native to Mexico.
funFact: It's named after Joel Poinsett, the first US minister to Mexico, who brought it to America in the 1820s.

question: In Home Alone, what nickname do burglars Harry and Marv give themselves?
hint: Marv leaves the same messy “calling card” at every house they rob.
funFact: In Home Alone 2, they rebrand as the Sticky Bandits.

question: In Love Actually, how does Mark silently tell Juliet he loves her on her doorstep?
hint: A stereo plays “Silent Night” while he stands there without saying a word.
funFact: Mark is played by Andrew Lincoln, later Rick Grimes on The Walking Dead.

question: In Christmas Vacation, instead of a Christmas bonus, Clark Griswold gets a membership to what?
answer: The Jelly of the Month Club
hint: Cousin Eddie calls it “the gift that keeps on giving the whole year.”
funFact: Clark had already put down a deposit on a backyard swimming pool, counting on that bonus.

question: Which actor plays a wisecracking, cool-as-ice Santa in Netflix's The Christmas Chronicles (2018)?
hint: He starred in Escape from New York and Tombstone.
funFact: His real-life partner, Goldie Hawn, surprises viewers with a cameo as Mrs. Claus.

question: In Gremlins, Billy gets a furry mogwai for Christmas. What must you never do to it after midnight?
hint: It's not about water or bright light; those are the other two rules.
funFact: Gremlins was one of the movies that led to the PG-13 rating being created in 1984.

question: In Die Hard (1988), John McClane fights off terrorists during a Christmas Eve party at which fictional Los Angeles skyscraper?
hint: It's named after the Japanese company that owns it.
funFact: The real building is Fox Plaza in Century City, which is also 20th Century Fox's headquarters.

question: Snow looks white, but what color is a single ice crystal of a snowflake really?
hint: Think of a windowpane.
funFact: Snow looks white because its countless crystal surfaces bounce all colors of sunlight back at you, the same reason crushed glass looks white.

question: Which band recorded the 1963 Christmas hit “Little Saint Nick”?
hint: This California group is famous for surf songs and sunny harmonies.
funFact: The song describes Santa's sleigh like a souped-up hot rod, a favorite subject of the band's car songs.

question: Which former Beatle released “Happy Xmas (War Is Over)” in 1971?
hint: He also wrote “Imagine.”
funFact: It grew out of John and Yoko's 1969 billboard campaign: “WAR IS OVER! If You Want It.”

question: “Let It Snow! Let It Snow! Let It Snow!” was written in 1945 during what kind of weather?
hint: It was July in Hollywood.
funFact: The lyrics never actually mention Christmas.

question: Besides marshmallows for toasting, what kind of stories does “It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year” promise?
hint: Something you'd normally expect at Halloween.
funFact: Telling ghost stories at Christmas was a popular Victorian tradition.

question: Which Canadian crooner's 2011 album “Christmas” was so huge that memes joke he “thaws out” every November?
hint: His hits include “Haven't Met You Yet” and “Home.”
funFact: It was the second best-selling album of 2011 in the US, behind only Adele's “21.”

question: In A Charlie Brown Christmas (1965), which character takes the stage to explain the true meaning of Christmas?
hint: He's never without his security blanket.
funFact: The special won an Emmy and a Peabody Award.

question: In the very first full episode of The Simpsons (1989), the family adopts a dog on Christmas Eve. What is his name?
hint: He's a racing greyhound who finished dead last.
funFact: The episode, “Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire,” aired on December 17, 1989.

question: In The Office, which Dunder Mifflin employee dresses up as Belsnickel for a Pennsylvania Dutch Christmas?
hint: He's a beet farmer and Assistant (to the) Regional Manager.
funFact: Belsnickel is a real fur-clad gift-bringer from German and Pennsylvania Dutch folklore.

question: In which country is a bucket of KFC a hugely popular Christmas dinner?
hint: There, Christmas Eve is more of a festive date night than a religious holiday.
funFact: It started with KFC's 1974 “Kentucky for Christmas” campaign, and families now order weeks ahead.

question: In Alpine folklore, what horned, half-goat creature punishes naughty children at Christmastime?
hint: He travels with St. Nicholas, carrying chains and a bundle of sticks.
funFact: On Krampusnacht, December 5, costumed Krampuses parade through towns in Austria and Bavaria.

question: Rovaniemi, which calls itself the “Official Hometown of Santa Claus,” is in which country?
hint: It's in Lapland, right on the Arctic Circle.
funFact: Its Santa Claus Village draws hundreds of thousands of visitors a year, and you can meet Santa there any day.

question: What is the holiday on December 26 called in the UK, Canada and Australia?
hint: It's a big day for shopping sales and sports.
funFact: The name is thought to come from the “Christmas boxes” of money or gifts once given to servants and tradespeople.

question: What do Germans call the hot spiced wine sold at their Christmas markets?
hint: It's often served in a souvenir mug.
funFact: Its name literally means “glow wine.”

question: What tall, dome-shaped Italian sweet bread, studded with candied fruit and raisins, comes from Milan?
hint: Its name means “large loaf” in Italian.
funFact: Bakers cool it upside down so the airy dome doesn't collapse.

question: Which French Christmas dessert is a rolled sponge cake covered in chocolate “bark” and often topped with meringue mushrooms?
hint: It's shaped like a piece of firewood.
funFact: It recalls the old custom of burning a huge Yule log on the hearth at Christmas.

question: Many Italian-American families celebrate Christmas Eve with the “Feast of the Seven…” what?
hint: Meat is traditionally skipped that night.
funFact: It grew out of the Catholic custom of not eating meat on Christmas Eve, and many families call it La Vigilia.

question: The famous Christmas Truce, when enemy soldiers sang carols and swapped gifts in no man's land, happened during which war?
hint: Soldiers faced each other from muddy trenches.
funFact: It began on Christmas Eve 1914, and some accounts describe British and German soldiers playing football (soccer) together.

question: When the Soviet Union brought back the banned Christmas tree in 1935, which holiday was it decorated for instead?
hint: It's still the biggest winter celebration in Russia.
funFact: In Russia, Ded Moroz (“Grandfather Frost”) still brings presents at New Year.

question: In 1882, Edison's business partner Edward H. Johnson lit the first electrically lit Christmas tree. What three colors were its 80 bulbs?
hint: Think of a patriotic color scheme.
funFact: Before electric lights, people clipped real lit candles onto their tree branches.

question: What natural chemical makes Christmas peppermint treats feel cool in your mouth?
hint: It's also in cough drops and chest rubs.
funFact: It tricks your cold-sensing nerves into firing, so your mouth feels cool even though nothing got colder.

question: Unlike nearly all other deer, female reindeer also grow what?
hint: Bony headgear that's shed and regrown every year.
funFact: Males shed theirs after the autumn mating season while females keep theirs through winter, which led to the playful theory that Santa's reindeer are female.

question: What British Christmas table favorite is a paper tube two people pull until it bangs, spilling out a paper crown, a joke and a toy?
hint: It shares its name with a crunchy snack you'd eat with cheese.
funFact: London confectioner Tom Smith is credited with inventing them in the 1840s; they started out as wrapped sweets, and the bang came later.

question: Queen Victoria's husband helped make the Christmas tree fashionable in Britain in the 1840s. What was his name?
hint: He was born in Germany.
funFact: When an American magazine reprinted an 1848 picture of the royal family around their tree, it erased Victoria's tiara and Albert's mustache to make them look American.

question: Canada Post gives Santa his very own postal code. What is it?
hint: It's a pun on his famous laugh.
funFact: Santa gets about a million letters a year through Canada Post, and each one is answered in the language it was written in.

question: In The Elf on the Shelf, what is the one thing children must never do to the scout elf, or it could lose its magic?
hint: It involves your hands.
funFact: Carol Aebersold and her daughter Chanda Bell self-published the book in 2005.

question: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer was created in 1939 as a free giveaway booklet for which department store chain?
hint: A Chicago mail-order catalog company founded in 1872.
funFact: Copywriter Robert L. May wrote it, and the store gave away about 2.4 million copies the first year.

question: In The Muppet Christmas Carol (1992), which Oscar-winning British actor plays Scrooge?
hint: He played Alfred the butler in the Dark Knight films.
funFact: It was the first Muppet movie made after Jim Henson's death, and his son Brian directed it.

question: Count every gift in every verse of “The Twelve Days of Christmas,” repeats included (the partridge alone arrives 12 times). What's the grand total?
hint: It's somewhere between 300 and 400.
funFact: That's one gift for every day of the year, minus one.

question: In the 1970 stop-motion special Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town, which legendary dancer narrates as the mailman?
hint: He danced “Cheek to Cheek” with Ginger Rogers.
funFact: Mickey Rooney voices Kris Kringle, the young toymaker who grows up to become Santa.

question: The “X” in “Xmas” isn't really an English letter. Which Greek letter is it?
hint: It's the first letter of “Christ” in Greek, and it rhymes with “sky.”
funFact: The abbreviation has been used in English since the 1500s, so it isn't a modern shortcut.

question: In the Netherlands, Sinterklaas arrives each November by steamboat from which country?
hint: A sunny southern European country famous for flamenco.
funFact: The name “Santa Claus” comes from Sinterklaas.

question: How many mischievous Yule Lads visit Icelandic children, one each night, in the days before Christmas?
hint: Think of a famously unlucky number.
funFact: Kids leave a shoe on the windowsill: good children get a treat, naughty ones get a potato.

question: Every Christmas Eve at 3 p.m., millions of Swedes watch an old cartoon special starring which Disney character?
hint: He wears a sailor shirt and no pants.
funFact: It has aired every Christmas Eve since 1960 and still draws around 3 million viewers in a country of about 10.5 million.

question: In Catalonia, kids “feed” a smiling object for weeks, then whack it with sticks at Christmas until it “poops” out sweets. What is it?
hint: It's made of wood and usually wears a little red hat.
funFact: It typically “poops” turrón (nougat) and other treats while the family sings a song ordering it to.

question: In Italy, which kindly old witch flies on her broomstick to bring children gifts on the eve of Epiphany?
hint: Her name comes from the Italian word for Epiphany.
funFact: Naughty children may get a lump of “coal,” often made of black sugar.

question: In December 1965, the Gemini 6A astronauts played “Jingle Bells” in orbit. One shook small bells; what instrument did the other play?
hint: A pocket-sized instrument you blow into.
funFact: The Smithsonian, which displays both, calls them the first musical instruments played in space; just before playing, the crew jokingly reported a UFO piloted by someone in a red suit.

question: What is the proper title of the poem better known as “’Twas the Night Before Christmas”?
accept: Account of a Visit from St. Nicholas
hint: It's a five-word title that names the poem's famous guest.
funFact: It first ran anonymously, as “Account of a Visit from St. Nicholas,” in the Troy Sentinel in December 1823; Clement Clarke Moore claimed it years later, though some argue Henry Livingston Jr. wrote it.

question: Which New York newspaper printed the famous 1897 editorial “Yes, Virginia, there is a Santa Claus”?
hint: One short word. Think astronomy.
funFact: Eight-year-old Virginia O'Hanlon wrote in to ask, and the reply became the most reprinted newspaper editorial in the English language.

question: The real St. Nicholas was a 4th-century bishop of Myra. In which modern-day country is Myra?
hint: Its largest city straddles Europe and Asia.
funFact: In 1087, sailors from Bari, Italy, carried off most of his bones, which still rest in Bari's Basilica of San Nicola.

question: From 1659 to 1681, celebrating Christmas was banned, with a five-shilling fine, in which American colony?
hint: Puritans ran this New England colony.
funFact: Historians have found no record of anyone actually being prosecuted under the law.

question: Reindeer eyes change color with the seasons: gold in summer, and what color in the dark Arctic winter?
hint: Think of a cold, icy color.
funFact: Scientists reported the change in 2013; it helps reindeer see in the near-constant darkness of an Arctic winter.

question: In the carol “O Tannenbaum,” what kind of evergreen does “Tannenbaum” literally mean in German?
hint: Its name has just three letters.
funFact: In German, “Tanne” means fir and “Baum” means tree.

question: Which 19th-century Harper's Weekly cartoonist drew dozens of Santa illustrations that shaped the jolly, bearded Santa we know today?
hint: His cartoons also took on New York's corrupt “Boss” Tweed.
funFact: His first Santa, published in January 1863, handed out gifts to Union soldiers in a Civil War camp.

question: In the 1974 TV special The Year Without a Santa Claus, which character forces the feuding Snow Miser and Heat Miser to compromise?
hint: She's their mom, and people blame her when a picnic gets rained out.
funFact: The squabbling Misers were such breakout stars that they got their own spin-off special in 2008, A Miser Brothers' Christmas.

question: Which hot spiced Christmas drink takes its name from an old toast meaning “be well” or “good health”?
hint: It's often made from hot cider or ale with apples and spices.
funFact: Wassailers went door to door singing and offering a drink from the wassail bowl in exchange for gifts, as in the carol “Here We Come A-wassailing.”

question: What German Christmas fruit bread, thickly dusted with powdered sugar, is celebrated with a giant version at a festival in Dresden?
hint: It often has a log of marzipan running through the middle.
funFact: Its shape and white sugar coating are said to represent the baby Jesus wrapped in swaddling clothes.

question: The gentle carol “Do You Hear What I Hear?” was written as a plea for peace during which Cold War crisis?
hint: It was written in October 1962.
funFact: The line “Pray for peace, people everywhere” reflects the fear of nuclear war that fall.

question: In White Christmas (1954), which comedian plays Bing Crosby's army buddy and song-and-dance partner?
hint: He played the daydreaming Walter Mitty in 1947.
funFact: Rosemary Clooney, who co-starred, was George Clooney's aunt.

question: Netflix's Oscar-nominated 2019 animated film tells how a lazy postman named Jesper and a reclusive toymaker started the Santa legend. What's the title?
hint: Its one-word title is a common German first name.
funFact: It won the BAFTA for Best Animated Film and seven Annie Awards, including Best Animated Feature.

question: In the 2024 action-comedy Red One, Dwayne Johnson and Chris Evans rescue a kidnapped Santa. Which actor plays Santa?
hint: He won an Oscar as a terrifying music teacher in Whiplash.
funFact: Bonnie Hunt plays Mrs. Claus.

question: In “Winter Wonderland,” the couple builds a snowman in the meadow and pretends he is who?
hint: His last name is a color.
funFact: A later, kid-friendly version of the lyric turned him into a circus clown.
